canonical_question: Does the 259.3 ± 19.2 GPa Young's modulus suggest a specific phase fraction or texture that differs from the DFT prediction of 229 GPa?

question_variants.question: Does the 259.3 ± 19.2 GPa Young's modulus suggest a specific phase fraction or texture that differs from the DFT prediction of 229 GPa?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The document reports the experimental Young's modulus (259.3 GPa) and DFT prediction (229 GPa) but does not discuss whether this difference implies a specific phase fraction or texture differing from the DFT model.

answers.answer: The text reports an average Young’s modulus of 259.3 ± 19.2 GPa experimentally, while the DFT-calculated mechanical properties showed a Young’s modulus of 229 GPa. The text does not attribute this discrepancy to a specific phase fraction or texture difference.
answers.measurement_outcome: experimental modulus 259.3 ± 19.2 GPa vs DFT 229 GPa
answers.boundary_limitation: no microstructural explanation provided for modulus difference
evidence_spans: In this work, a refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film of equimolar CuMoTaWV was deposited on silicon and 304 stainless-steel substrates using DC-magnetron sputtering.
A sputtering target was developed by partial sintering of an equimolar powder mixture of Cu, Mo, Ta, W, and V using spark plasma sintering.
The target was used to sputter a nanocrystalline RHEA film with a thickness of ∼900 nm and an average grain size of 18 nm.
